newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech crown still volatile, CNB battles on.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech crown still volatile, CNB battles on.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) again intervened to support the crown on Monday, as political uncertainty and more economic bad news kept market sentiment decidedly bearish against the currency.

The market opened on a volatile note as the first round of talks between Czech coalition parties on a cabinet reshuffle ended inconclusively, two days after the finance and interior ministers resigned.
The statistical bureau (CSU) then added to the instability when it released worse than expected April trade figures.

The crown, besieged over the past 10 days by a wave of foreign short-selling that pushed it to record lows against its dollar/mark basket, steadied by late morning at around 3.2 percent below basket parity.
But the central bank intervened late in the day to pull the crown back to around -2.0 percent, helped in part by thin activity as London and New York enjoyed banking holidays.
"Even without London and New York, the bearish pressure is still there, though not as strongly," said Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka.

Analysts said the political situation was one of the biggest factors driving the market, as discussions over the extent of the shake-up with coalition partners began after the two ministers stepped down on Saturday.

The leaders agreed to change the cabinet last week in order to answer a sharp drop in the centre-right government's approval ratings amid an economic downturn and a widespread feeling that financial crime is pervasive.

But Monday's meeting suggested agreement on the share-out of ministerial posts would be difficult. "We clearly indicated our mutual limits and the corridor within which we can move," Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told journalists after Monday's meeting.
"The only outcome (of Monday's talks) I can say is that the corridor which exists after today, if it was played to the finish line in this way, has a solution," he added.
He declined to elaborate, and party leaders set another meeting for noon on Tuesday.
The bears were fed further when the Statistical Bureau (CSU) released April trade data which was far below earlier estimates by Klaus.
The premier had said the April shortfall should end up at around 11.4 billion crowns ($376.6 million), but the CSU numbers put the gap at some 15.34 billion crowns.
"For the Prime Minister, this is kind of a shame. He said 11.4 billion crowns but the final figures are actually much higher," said Petr Kukla, a trader at Girocredit.
The crown has been under heavy downward pressure as the trade gap has caused an already large current account deficit to grow to more than nine percent of gross domestic product.
But the crown, which hit a record low against its dollar/mark basket midpoint of -6.4 percent last week, reacted indifferently to the data.
"The figures were disappointing, but there are so few crowns left in the market that we saw little effect," said another forex trader.

But warned Komercni's Becvar: "We may see a push lower again tomorrow...now it depends on the central bank's policy, and I think that the best option is still to widen the band of the crown," he added.
The CNB fixes the crown daily within a 7.5 percent fluctuation band on either side of its dollar/mark basket midpoint.
The central bank fixed the crown at 30.475 to the dollar and 18.078 to the mark on Monday, implying a deviation against basket parity of -2.80 percent after a fixing of -3.74 percent on Friday.
